chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan said: Muhammad al-Katib narrated to me from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Muawiya ibn Maythara ibn Shurayh, who said: My father Abdullah ibn Muawiya narrated to me from his father Maythara from his father Shurayh, who said: Maythara said

A woman approached Shurayh and said, 'I have come to you as a litigant.' He asked her, 'And where is your opponent?' She said, 'You are my opponent.' He cleared the session for her and said, 'Speak.' She said, 'I am a woman who has both a penis and a vagina.' He said, 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had a ruling in this matter: 'He inherits from where the urine comes from.' She said, 'It comes from both of them together.' He asked her, 'From where does the urine precede?' She said, 'Nothing from either precedes the urine; they come at one time and cease at one time.' He said to her, 'You are telling something amazing.' She said, 'I will tell you something more amazing than this: A cousin of mine married me, and I had a servant. I had intercourse with her and she bore me a child. I have come to you regarding what was born to me, so that you may separate me from my husband.'

He rose from the judicial session and entered upon Ali (peace be upon him) and informed him of what the woman had said. He ordered that she be brought in and asked her about what the judge had said. She said, 'It is what he informed you of.' He said, 'Then her husband, her cousin, was brought in.' Ali, Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), said to him, 'This is your wife and the daughter of your cousin.' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do you know what happened?' He said, 'Yes, I had her as a servant, had intercourse with her, and she bore me a child.' He said, 'Then did you have intercourse with her after that?' He said, 'Yes.'

Ali (peace be upon him) said to him, 'You are bolder than the eunuch of the lion, who demanded a dinar from me.' And he was considered reliable, 'and with two women.' They were brought to him, and he said to them, 'Take this woman, if she is a woman, bring her into a room, dress her in a veil, strip her of her clothes, and count the ribs of her two sides.' They did so, then came out to him and said, 'The count of the right side is twelve ribs, and the left side is eleven ribs.'
Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'God is the Greatest. Bring me the cupper.' He took some of her hair and gave her a cloak and sandals, and attached her to the men.

The husband said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, my wife and my cousin, you attached her to the men. From where did you take this ruling?' He said, 'I inherited it from my father Adam and my mother Hawwa. She was created from the rib of Adam, and the ribs of men are fewer than the ribs of women by one rib, and the number of her ribs is the ribs of a man.' He ordered them to be taken out.

key_terms.وَرَّثَ مِنْ حَيْثُ جَاءَ الْبَوْلُ: He inherits from where the urine comes from (a principle of gender determination)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali determine the gender of a hermaphrodite for inheritance and marriage purposes?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the juristic principle of *al-warith min haythu ja'a al-bawl* (inheritance follows the exit of urine), where Imam Ali (AS) utilized anatomical verification—counting ribs—to resolve the ambiguity of a hermaphrodite's gender for marital dissolution. By determining she possessed the male rib count (23), Ali (AS) classified her as male, thereby dissolving the marriage contract which was predicated on her being female, a ruling deeply rooted in Shia legal methodology regarding *khuntha* (hermaphrodite).
